comment: A global Reference Architecture should avoid mandating collection of personal attributes that are not universally necessary for identity resolution. Nationality and residence are distinct concepts and should not be represented as a single attribute. A mother's/guardian's name may be highly relevant to newborn identification but is not inherently necessary in every adult record; similarly, address and contact details may support matching in one jurisdiction but be unnecessary in another with a robust persistent identifier. Making such attributes universally mandatory could lead to avoidable collection and synchronisation of personal data. In Spain, the CIP-SNS is unique and lifelong and serves as the linking key between the regional identifiers assigned by different health administrations, allowing identity interoperability while preserving regional databases. This illustrates why the minimum identity dataset should be adapted to the identification architecture.

public.text: A global Reference Architecture should avoid mandating collection of personal attributes that are not universally necessary for identity resolution. Nationality and residence are distinct concepts and should not be represented as a single attribute. A mother's/guardian's name may be highly relevant to newborn identification but is not inherently necessary in every adult record; similarly, address and contact details may support matching in one jurisdiction but be unnecessary in another with a robust persistent identifier. Making such attributes universally mandatory could lead to avoidable collection and synchronisation of personal data. In Spain, the CIP-SNS is unique and lifelong and serves as the linking key between the regional identifiers assigned by different health administrations, allowing identity interoperability while preserving regional databases. This illustrates why the minimum identity dataset should be adapted to the identification architecture.
public.suggestedRevision: Revise the dataset classification so that attributes are mandatory only where systematically necessary for the jurisdiction's identity-resolution model. Specifically: (i) separate nationality/citizenship from country/place of residence; (ii) change address, contact information, local identifiers and mother's/guardian's name to Conditional unless needed for the applicable identity-resolution workflow; (iii) replace “where available and consented” for foundational identifiers with “where available, necessary and lawfully permitted under the applicable framework”; and (iv) state that jurisdictions using robust persistent identifiers may use a smaller mandatory demographic matching dataset.
